hints: Focus on oxidation numbers, not just on formulas. Track what happens to Fe and to Cr from left to right.
Check Fe first. It goes from $\text{FeSO}_4$ to $\text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$, so work out if +2 has gone to +3.
Now check oxygen carefully. It starts at -2 in sulfate and dichromate and ends at -2 in sulfate and water, so ask yourself if its oxidation number really changed.
walkthrough:
**Check the iron change**

Look at iron on both sides. It is lovely and simple.

On the left in $\text{FeSO}_4$: $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ is -2, so Fe is +2.
$$\text{Fe(II)} \rightarrow \text{Fe(III)}$$

**Confirm iron is oxidised**

On the right in $\text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$: $3 \times (-2) = -6$, so $2 \times \text{Fe} = +6$ and Fe is +3.

Increase in oxidation number from +2 to +3 means loss of electrons, so statement 1 is true:
$$\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + e^-$$

**Check the chromium change**

Now look at $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ on the left. Na is +1 and O is -2.

So $2(+1) + 2(\text{Cr}) + 7(-2) = 0$, giving Cr = +6.
$$\text{Cr(VI) in dichromate}$$

**Confirm chromium is reduced**

On the right in $\text{Cr}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$: $3 \times (-2) = -6$, so $2 \times \text{Cr} = +6$ and Cr is +3.

Decrease from +6 to +3 means gain of electrons, so statement 2 is true:
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test the oxygen claim**

This is the clever trap. Oxygen looks like it makes water, but check its oxidation number.

In $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, in $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ and in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, oxygen is -2 throughout. No change in oxidation number means no redox change for oxygen, so statement 3 is false.

True statements are 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes statement 3. Oxygen stays at oxidation number -2 in sulfate, in dichromate and in water, so it is not reduced. It is just transferred to form water to balance H+ and O.
options.B: Correct because statements 1 and 2 only are true. Fe(II) to Fe(III) is oxidation by loss of one electron, and Cr(VI) to Cr(III) is reduction by gain of three electrons per Cr. Oxygen does not change oxidation number.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes statement 3 and omits statement 1. Statement 1 is clearly true from $\text{FeSO}_4$ to $\text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$, while statement 3 is false since O remains -2.
options.D: Incorrect because it omits statement 2. Cr definitely changes from +6 in $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ to +3 in $\text{Cr}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$, which is the reduction that balances the oxidation of iron.
